item.title: EU Right to Repair Directive Goes Live July 31
item.description: EU’s Right to Repair directive takes effect July 31, 2026, mandating free repair manuals, reasonable pricing, and extended warranties for household and tech devices.

item.title: EU Mandates AI-Generated Content Labels Starting Aug 2
item.description: Starting Aug 2, the EU AI Act requires AI‑generated images, audio and text that look real to carry digital watermarks, with fines up to 3% of revenue.

item.title: Can Republicans Really Send Fauci to Jail Now?
item.description: Explore the legal battle over Fauci’s Fifth Amendment rights, presidential pardons, and the Senate’s contempt powers amid a high‑stakes Covid‑19 inquiry.

item.title: NY Attorney General Sues Kalshi for Illegal Gambling
item.description: NY AG Letitia James sues Kalshi, alleging the platform runs an illegal gambling operation without a state license, endangering users and minors.

item.title: Apple Settles Siri AI Delay Lawsuit for $250M
item.description: Apple gains preliminary court approval for a $250 million settlement, offering up to $95 per eligible iPhone owner after the delayed Siri AI launch.

item.title: Apple vs OpenAI: Trade Secrets Suit Moves to New Judge
item.description: Apple’s high‑profile trade‑secrets lawsuit against OpenAI has been reassigned to a new federal judge, raising stakes for AI IP protection and industry dynamics.

item.title: Apple’s $250 Million Siri Settlement Approved
item.description: Apple’s $250 million Siri privacy settlement has been approved, detailing the payout structure and its ripple effects across tech, law, and AI.

item.title: EPA Rule May Mute Public Voice on Data Center Emissions
item.description: The EPA’s proposed rule shift could hand permitting power to states, letting gas plants and data‑center generators bypass public notice and comment.

item.title: Trump Endorses MyPillow Founder for Minnesota Governor
item.description: Donald Trump backs MyPillow founder Mike Lindell for Minnesota governor, sparking backlash over his finances, lack of experience, and electability.

item.title: EU Says TikTok Must Make Child Safety Opt‑Out, Not Opt‑In
item.description: EU DSA review flags TikTok’s default public accounts, For You feed recommendations, and private‑account discoverability, urging opt‑out child safety.

item.title: Tesla Door Handle Issue Could Trigger New Safety Rules
item.description: NHTSA says Tesla’s door‑release complaints don’t merit a defect probe, but a new rule could force all automakers to add robust door‑egress systems.

item.title: Why Apple Excluded Jony Ive from Its OpenAI Lawsuit
item.description: Apple left Jony Ive out of its $6.5 billion OpenAI trade‑secret suit, hinting at Laurene Powell Jobs' influence and the company's hardware push.

item.title: EU Slaps AliExpress with Record $629M DSA Fine
item.description: The European Commission fines AliExpress €550 million for non‑compliance with the Digital Services Act, highlighting platform safety and EU enforcement.

item.title: EU Slaps AliExpress with Record $625M DSA Fine
item.description: EU Commission fines AliExpress $625 million under the DSA for not removing counterfeit and unsafe goods, forcing a new era of e‑commerce compliance.
